title: Rollout telemetry fusion and granular cohort diff workbench
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a workbench in Console that fuses per-route telemetry (latency P50/P95, token cost, error rates), trace-linked sample requests, and cohort-diff visualizations so PMs/SEs can quickly reason about regressions during canary, A/B, and shadow experiments.

Background: Customers rely on per-route rollouts and often need to compare two cohorts (e.g., canary vs baseline, or variant A vs B) by multiple dimensions simultaneously — request shape, latency distribution, semantic divergence, and cost. Existing panels surface single metrics or list traces but lack: (1) synchronized cohort filters, (2) trace linkage from diff outliers, and (3) a lightweight rollback simulator that estimates user impact for an automatic fallback.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: cohort diff canvas with multi-metric anchors, heatmap of divergence by traffic slice, trace drilldown that links to spans and request payloads, per-route cost delta, and a scenario simulator that projects impact of reverting or shifting traffic. Includes backend telemetry fusion APIs and frontend workbench UX.
- Out-of-scope: automatic rollback execution (this ticket only provides simulation & recommendation hooks), full audit logging for private deployments (audit integration in follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console shows side-by-side cohort summaries for selected time windows and routes with computed deltas (latency P50/P95, error rate, token-cost-per-request) and allows pinning filters that apply across all panels.
2) Users can select an outlier cell in the diff heatmap and open 3 representative traces (sampled) with span view and input/response payload links.
3) Rollback simulator accepts simple knobs (percent traffic shift, time horizon) and returns projected impacted requests, cost delta, and estimated service-level delta with confidence bands.
4) New telemetry fusion APIs published in Redwood internal spec and covered by integration tests and a staging dashboard.
5) UX flows reviewed by Design and validated with 2 customer interviews (SaaS and Enterprise platform team).

Constraints and implementation notes:
- Telemetry fusion layer will join time-series metrics, per-request traces, and the cohort attribution table in the Console read model via a new rollup job; aim for query latencies < 500ms for common slices.
- Sampling budget: ensure traces for a cohort sample are representative; use stratified sampler by route + latency bucket.
- Privacy: redact PII in request payloads returned to Console.

Open decisions:
- Whether the rollback simulator should run using production SLO thresholds or only using delta heuristics (decision due by 2025-03-05).
- How to express semantic divergence: cosine distance on embeddings vs n-gram/length heuristics (performance vs interpretability trade-off).
comments: 2025-02-10: Kickoff with Eng and Design. Agreed to prototype cohort anchoring UX before backend contract is finalized. Action: Design to produce a microflow by 2025-02-14. (Ava)
2025-02-14: Design review — microflow and two wireframes attached. Feedback: add a compact heatmap legend and a ‘compare by token-cost’ toggle. (Design: Priya Kapoor)

2025-02-20: Eng scoping meeting — backend will expose /console/rollouts/fusion API; initial PR created ENG-27411. Trade-off: precompute cohort deltas for recent 24h windows to meet latency target; historical full-window queries will be async. (Lead Eng: Marcus Li)

2025-02-28: Customer research — interviewed CloudShelf (SaaS) and FinancialPlatformX (enterprise). Both want trace linkage and rollback impact estimator. FinancialPlatformX requested audited reasoning for any auto-rollback recommendation. (Ava)

2025-03-04: Decision: Fall back to cosine embedding divergence as the first MVP metric for semantic drift with a plan to add lightweight n-gram signals later. Recorded as design decision in doc. (PM + ML Research)
2025-03-10: UX walkthrough with Console team. Minor change: move 'Simulator' panel to secondary dock to encourage manual review before acting. (Design approval pending)
2025-03-11: Integration test checklist added to PR template and a staging dashboard created at /dash/rollout-fusion/staging. (Eng)

2025-03-12: Blocker noted — sampling budget leads to sparse traces for low-volume routes. Mitigation: stratified sampler and a fallback of synthetic request clustering for representative traces. (Marcus)
2025-03-12: Next steps: finish backend integration for cohort deltas (ENG-27411), finalize design assets, schedule two customer validation sessions week of 2025-03-17. (Ava)
Review links: Confluence spec (docs.redwood.com/display/RO/rollout-telemetry-fusion), GitHub PR (github.com/redwood/console/pull/9123), Staging dashboard (/dash/rollout-fusion/staging)
notes: Prototype must demonstrate sub-500ms query for common cohort slices in staging and include a short runbook describing how PMs should interpret simulator output when considering manual rollback.
